saints.name: St. Valerian of Abbenza
saints.title: Bishop and Confessor
saints.shortBlurb: An aged African bishop who, rather than surrender the goods of the Church to the Arian Vandals, was cast out to die in the open road…
biography: Valerian was bishop of Abbenza in Roman Africa when Genseric, the Arian king of the Vandals, persecuted the Catholic Church in the fifth century. About the year 457 the king's deputy Proculus was sent through the province to strip the churches, and the bishops who would not surrender their sacred vessels and books were driven from their sees.

Valerian, though more than eighty years old, refused to deliver up the vessels of his church, and was cast out alone beyond the city. By the king's command no man might receive him into house or field, and so the aged bishop lay long in the public road under the open sky, until he ended his days — a confessor, for he bore his passion for the faith without the shedding of blood.

His witness was recorded by the contemporary historian Victor of Vita, who wrote the history of that persecution, and the Roman Martyrology keeps his memory on 15 December: an old man faithful unto death, a confessor of the orthodox truth.
saints.knownFor: An aged confessor of the faith under the Arian Vandal persecution.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
